subject_line: Weekly Google Ads brief: 56 leads at $58, heating leads the way | Week of Oct 12

body.headline: A steady week: 56 leads at $58 each, down 7% on last week and 11% under the $65 target. Heating is carrying the account; AC installation still costs far more per lead than anything else.

scorecard.compared_with: Oct 5-Oct 11 and the 4 weeks before Oct 12

rows.vs_target: on track for $14,186 against the $14,000 monthly budget

wins: Furnace Repair brought 14 leads at $63 each, against 14 the week before, as more people searched for heating help.
Plumbing brought 9 leads at $60 each, against 9 the week before.
Your cost per lead (CPA, what each call or booking costs) came in at $58, +7% on last week and +9% on the 4-week average.
concerns: AC Installation spent $349 with no leads this week, the most spend above target. Plan: we added a new ad on Oct 15 and will review its searches; if it stays this costly, we'll ask you about moving part of its budget to heating.

A new negative keyword, "cost", went into Water Heaters on Oct 14. It now blocks searches such as "tankless water heater cost", which brought leads before. Plan: we'll narrow it this week so price searches can show again.
context: Furnace Repair keeps losing about a fifth of its possible impressions because its budget runs out, so it has room to grow.
Brand searches, people looking for your company by name, brought 14 leads at $9 each, the same as the week before; they mostly reflect demand the ads didn't create.
Plumbing delivered 9 leads at $60, and Water Heaters 7 at $58: both steady and both under target.
The last two days may still gain a few late-credited calls and form fills.

changes: new responsive search ad in AC installation

what_changed.method_note: These before-and-after reads compare the same weekdays a week apart. They show what moved after a change, not proof that the change caused it.
what_changed.last_week_text: Last week's change, the AC Repair budget cut from $110 to $90 a day on Oct 6, had its first full week: spend went $485 to $426 and leads 6 to 5, so the smaller budget is holding.

campaign_highlights.top_performer: Top performer: Brand, with 14 leads at $9. It beats the target and still runs out of budget on busy days, which is the case for giving it more (see approvals).
campaign_highlights.needs_attention: Needs attention: AC Installation, the largest spend above target. Searches for new units are early research, so leads are slow and costly.

completed_this_week: Furnace Repair | Search, Oct 13: added 2 negative keywords: "diy", "parts"
AC Installation | Search, Oct 15: new responsive search ad in AC installation
AC Repair | Search, Oct 16: target CPA $75 -> $70
Water Heaters | Search, Oct 14: added the broad negative "cost"
planned_next_week: Narrow the "cost" negative in Water Heaters so converting price searches return.
Review AC Installation's search terms and its new ad's first week.
Check Furnace Repair's lost impressions again on Monday.
Compare this week's leads with your booking records, so we can see which campaigns bring paying jobs and not only calls.
needs_your_approval: Move $30 a day from AC Installation (no leads for $349 this week) to Furnace Repair (about $63 a lead). Extra budget usually costs more per lead than today's average, so expect the new leads to cost a little more than $63.

projection.label: straight-line estimate: spend so far / 18 days x 31

pacing.text: October so far: $8,237 spent for 146 leads through Oct 18. At this pace the month lands near $14,186, within the $14,000 budget.

tracking_check.read: Each counted lead type moved in line with total leads, and none started or stopped counting this week.

body.closing: A steady week led by heating. One decision for you: the $30-a-day move from AC Installation to Furnace Repair.
